overview: This Senate resolution mourns the death of former President Jimmy Carter, the 39th president, who lived to 100, longer than any other president. It reviews his life, from his Navy service and Georgia peanut farm to his terms as a Georgia state senator and governor and his presidency from 1977 to 1981. It highlights the Camp David Accords between Egypt and Israel, the creation of the Departments of Education and Energy, and his later humanitarian work through The Carter Center, including efforts against Guinea worm disease and election monitoring. The Senate extends its sympathies to his family and honors his legacy. It was cosponsored by nearly the whole Senate and approved by unanimous consent on January 9, 2025.
for: Supporters say it is fitting for the Senate to honor a former president's lifetime of public and humanitarian service.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
